\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آفت} (āfat)}{آفت (āfat)}]{\ur{آفت} (āfat) — a disaster; a calamity}

\label{lesson:UR-C290-afat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to melt, then the Urdu for to rush in a panic.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آفت}}
\textbf{\ur{آفت}} — \emph{āfat} — \textquotedblleft{}a disaster; a calamity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{ایک} \ur{بڑی} \ur{آفت} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih ek baṛī āfat thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This was a great disaster.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{آفت}} (\emph{āfat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{āfa}, \textquotedblleft{}a blight, a misfortune\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine: \textbf{\ur{بڑی} \ur{آفت}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āfat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āfat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yih ek baṛī āfat thī.} — This was a great disaster.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to melt, then the Urdu for to rush in a panic, then say \emph{āfat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{آفت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A disaster; a calamity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اعلان} (elān)}{اعلان (elān)}]{\ur{اعلان} (elān) — an announcement}

\label{lesson:UR-C290-elan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to rush in a panic, then the Urdu for a disaster.

\textbf{\ur{اعلان}} — \emph{elān} — \textquotedblleft{}an announcement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zarā suniye, ek elān hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Masculine.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خطرہ} (khatrā)}{خطرہ (khatrā)}]{\ur{خطرہ} (khatrā) — a danger}

\label{lesson:UR-C290-khatra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a disaster, then the Urdu for an announcement.

\textbf{\ur{خطرہ}} — \emph{khatrā} — \textquotedblleft{}a danger\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Masculine.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹلنا} (ṭalnā)}{ٹلنا (ṭalnā)}]{\ur{ٹلنا} (ṭalnā) — to be averted; to pass off}

\label{lesson:UR-C290-ttalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an announcement, then the Urdu for a danger.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹلنا}} — \emph{ṭalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be averted; to pass off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{خطرہ} \ur{ٹل} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khatrā ṭal gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The danger passed.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{خطرہ} \ur{ٹل} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh khatrā ṭal gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹلنا}} (\emph{ṭalnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ṭalnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to pass by, to be displaced\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{ṭálati} (CDIAL 5450). A danger that \textbf{\ur{ٹل} \ur{گیا}} moved off without striking.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{احتیاط} (ehtiyāt)}{احتیاط (ehtiyāt)}]{\ur{احتیاط} (ehtiyāt) — caution; care}

\label{lesson:UR-C290-ehtiyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a danger, then the Urdu for to be averted.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{احتیاط}}
\textbf{\ur{احتیاط}} — \emph{ehtiyāt} — \textquotedblleft{}caution; care\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سڑک} \ur{پر} \ur{احتیاط} \ur{سے} \ur{چلیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{saṛak par ehtiyāt se chaliye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Walk carefully on the road.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{احتیاط}} (\emph{ehtiyāt}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{iḥtiyāṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}caution, taking care\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{احتیاط} \ur{سے}} is carefully.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
